bio:
Servatius Birkenmayer was born at Munzingen, near Freiburg im Breisgau in Baden, on 4 May 1807, the son of Johann Birkenmayer, an official in the service of the manor, and Magdalena Erb. His marriage record gives the year as 1807, while his age at death implies 1806; 1807 is the better supported. His May birth fits his name, since the feast of St. Servatius falls on 13 May.

On 17 October 1836, by then a master glazier and citizen of Munzingen, he married Maria Agatha Heizler, born there on 26 June 1813, the daughter of the late Joseph Heizler, a huntsman in the manor's service, and Maria Anna Federer. The witnesses were Josef Ott, a farmer, and Johann Federer, formerly a glazier and by then a farmer. Their children included Joseph, born at Munzingen on 15 March 1842, who died at Sandusky, Ohio, in 1904, and Maria Anna, John's ancestor. Servatius was recorded as a glazier in 1837, as a citizen and glazier in 1842, and at his death as master joiner, cabinetmaker and glazier.

He died at Munzingen on 19 April 1853, aged 46, having received the last sacraments, and was buried on 21 April; the witnesses were his brother-in-law Friedrich Heizler, the gravedigger, and Johann Schell, a teacher. His toddler son Heinrich died about three weeks later. Later parish entries of 1862 and 1867 still remembered him as 'the late citizen and joiner Servatius Birkenmaier'. His widow Agatha died in 1867.

researchNotes:
Servatius Birkenmayer was born at Munzingen on 4 May 1807 (per his 1836 marriage; his death age, 46 years 11 months 15 days, implies 4 May 1806 — unresolved, 1807 preferred as the tree and marriage agree). His May birth fits the round-1 tip that St. Servatius's feast is 13 May. On 17 Oct 1836 at Munzingen (1836 Act. III): 'Servatius Birkenmayer, lediger Sohn des Johann Birkenmayer, herrschaftl. Waibel[?], und der + Magdalena Erb, nunmehr bürgerlicher Glasermeister, dahier geboren den 4ten May 1807' married 'M[aria] Agatha Heizler, ledige Tochter des + Joseph Heizler, herrschaftlicher Jäger, und der M. Anna Federer von hier, dahier geboren den 26ten Juny 1813'; witnesses Josef Ott, farmer, and Johann Federer, 'formerly glazier, now farmer'; licensed by the Grand-ducal Landamt Freiburg 11 Oct 1836, No. 19140; the 1836 index lists 'I. Birkenmayer Servatius mit Agatha Heizler'. (The FamilySearch index gives the marriage as 27 Oct 1836; the original reading 17 Oct is preferred.) He was a 'Glaser' in 1837, 'Bürger und Glaser' in 1842, and at death 'Schreiner- und Glasermeister u. Bürger' (master joiner/cabinetmaker and glazier). He died 19 Apr 1853 at Munzingen (No. 8), buried 21 Apr, having received the last sacraments; witnesses Friedrich Heizler, gravedigger (his brother-in-law), and Johann Schell, teacher. His toddler Heinrich died about three weeks later. Round 1 and 2 searched for him in vain: Kirchzarten parish database (~30,000 people, ~90 Neuhäuser Birkenmaiers) has no Servatius; GEDBAS and WikiTree have none. Round 2 found an Ancestry index naming Servatius Birkenmayer and 'Agatha Heitzler' as parents of Joseph Birkenmeier (b. 15 Mar 1842 Münzingen, d. Sandusky OH 1904), which led to the Munzingen registers. Nothing ties him to the 1848–49 revolution (he was 41 in 1848). Ancestry tree: 'Servatius Birkenmay… 1807–1853' + 'Maria A Heitzler 1813–1867'.

Two later Munzingen entries describe him after his death in the same way. In 1862 he is 'the late citizen and joiner (Schreiner) Servatius Birkenmaier', father of Maria Anna ([R4-S1]). In 1867 he is 'the late citizen and joiner Servaz Birkenmaier', husband of the widow Agatha ([R4-S2]). Neither entry adds a date.
